questionText:
Consider the following processor design characteristics.

I. Register-to-register arithmetic operations only
II. Fixed-length instruction format
III. Hardwired control unit

Which of the characteristics above are used in the design of a RISC processor?
explanation:
Characteristics of RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) processors:

1. Register-to-register arithmetic operations (Load/Store Architecture): In RISC processors, memory access is restricted to load and store instructions. All arithmetic and logic operations operate exclusively on register operands.

2. Fixed-length instruction format: Instructions are generally of uniform fixed size (e.g., 32-bit), which simplifies decoding and allows instruction execution to be easily pipelined.

3. Hardwired control unit: Hardwired control unit logic is used rather than microprogrammed control to maximize execution speed and minimize cycle times.

Therefore, all three statements (I, II, and III) are key design characteristics of a RISC processor.
